page: Google Cloud Platform x5-1376-24t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance featuring 1,376 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 24,576 GB of RAM. Designed without virtualization overhead, the physical platform delivers a memory-to-vCPU ratio of approximately 17.86 GB per core, targeting scenarios that require massive monolithic memory capacity.

The server contains no integrated local storage and no GPU accelerators, necessitating network-based persistent storage for stateful services. Operating as a bare-metal deployment removes hypervisor jitter, ensuring direct hardware control across all 1,376 dedicated execution threads.

From an infrastructure perspective, this instance prioritizes extreme vertical scale over distributed computing nodes, maximizing compute and RAM density in a single footprint. Appropriate workloads include enterprise in-memory databases, massive real-time caching architectures, SAP HANA, and large-scale analytical processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform x5-1376-24t-metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server equipped with 1,376 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs and 24,576 GB of system RAM. With a memory-to-core allocation of 17.86 GB per vCPU, it is configured for memory-intensive environments that exceed standard virtualized instance bounds. The platform includes no local disk storage and lacks integrated GPU acceleration, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data. By utilizing bare-metal hardware, the instance eliminates hypervisor overhead across its 1,376 execution threads, providing deterministic performance for extreme-scale computing. From an architectural efficiency perspective, the high density of memory and dedicated compute allows massive operational consolidation into a single host system. It is specifically targeted at enterprise in-memory databases, real-time transactional processing engines, and large-scale in-memory analytical workloads requiring substantial monolithic RAM capacity.
